previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after a mechanical fall from a toilet, presenting with left foot pain and symptoms of a urinary tract infection, including dysuria and fevers. Imaging confirmed a nondisplaced proximal fifth metatarsal fracture, managed conservatively with a splint and weight-bearing as tolerated. Urine culture grew ESBL-producing Escherichia coli, prompting treatment with IV meropenem initially, followed by a planned course of outpatient IV ertapenem via a midline catheter. The patient also exhibited indirect hyperbilirubinemia, which trended downward during admission and was deemed non-hemolytic and non-hepatic in origin. Chronic conditions, including HIV, hepatitis B and C, heart failure, and anticoagulation for prior DVT, were managed without complication. She remained afebrile, with stable vital signs, and was discharged home with home health services for antibiotic administration and clear follow-up instructions, including podiatry evaluation, INR monitoring, and a chest CT for a persistent lung opacity.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ HIV last CD4 792, VL undetectable, Hep C, dCHF, presents 
with 10lb weight gain, ___ edema, chest tightness x 1 week.  
  
# Urinary Tract Infection: The patient endorsed on admission 
sensations of dysuria. Her U/A in the ED showed nitrite 
positive, leuk positive, with WBCs and many leuks. Ultimately 
her urine culture came back as an ESBL; she has been treated for 
ESBL UTI, but notably several months ago had an episode of 
sepsis as a result, requiring an ICU stay. Given her risk 
factors such as HIV as well the aggressiveness of her UTI, she 
was started on Meropenam therapy (had initally recieved a dose 
of Bactrim in the ED). She was ultimately discharged from the 
hospital after threatening to leave against medical advice as a 
PICC line for her could not be placed on the anticipated day of 
discharge. Ultimately, an appointment was made for the patient 
the next morning to have a PICC line placed, and nursing teams 
perfomred teaching regarding the administration of ertapenam; 
the patient will plan to take a combined 10 day course of 
meropenam (which she toolk while int he hosptial) and ertapenam 
(which she will take a home given its once daily dosing). her 
symptoms improved while she was prsent in the hosptial on 
antiobitics. 

# Edema, weight gain: The patient endorses a 10 pound weight 
gain over the past week, which she says may secondary to a 
dietary indescretion as the result of somebody who had cooked 
for her. In the ED, her LLE was ruled out for a DVT, and the 
patient's legs were noted to have pitting edema. Cellulitis was 
not felt a likely culprit given the lack of systemic symptoms as 
well as findings on the leg that are not deep and red and warm, 
as one might expect with a cellulitis. The patient was treated 
with IV Furosemide 80 mg IV for two days, and then 80 mg PO for 
one day, and in total diuresed off nearly 25 pounds, after which 
she said her legs felt symptomatically improved. The cause of 
her edema was felt likely to right sided heart failure, almost 
certainly secondary to the patient's known diagnosis and poorly 
compliant treatment for OSA. She has a CPAP machine at home, but 
does not use it, and may benefit from further work-up by 
pulmonary in order to provide her with a more comfort-fitting 
mask. Creatinine never rose with IV duresis, but there was some 
concern with a slight elevation in bicarbon on HD#2 to 33, which 
subsequently resolved. Heart failure per se was not felt to be a 
likely etiology of her edema, given the fact that she did not 
have an elevated BNP, and CXR did not show any evidence of 
pulmonary congestion.

# History of DVT: Felt less likely during hosptialization given 
her negative DVT study, as well as the fact that on admission 
she was theraptuic on her warfarin at 2.8. INR was 
subtherapeutic the last two days of her admission, likely 
secondary to the fact that the ___ day of her admission, her 
home dose of warfarin was halved to 5 mg daily (as we had 
started antiobitcs that may have interferred with warfarin 
metabolism) The subsequent dsyas of her stay were cahcterized by 
warfarin at her home dosing. On discharge her INR 1.8. 

# Chest pain: The patient did not have any EKG changes from 
prior, and was tropinin negative x 3. Pain is likely secondary 
to anxiety, given clean coronaries on cath in ___. The pateint 
also recently had an ECHO without signs of FWM abnormality. Her 
pain was felt most likely secondary to anxiety and depression, 
and she was reassured and continued on her home antidepressants 
and anxiolytics.

# Right shoulder pain: The patient had fallen on her right 
shoulder approixmately one week prior to her admission; on exam, 
she had ful range of motions, and right shoulder films did not 
reveal any evidence of an acute fracture. She was continued on 
her home pain control, but may benefit from an outpateitn 
evaluation by orthopedics if her pain does not improve. 

# Elevated LFTs: Likely secondary to known underlying liver 
diases and cirrhosis, but alkphos was stable ___ at 130 
from ___ of this year, and Tbili had trended dwon to 1.6 from 
2.8 on ___.
  
# HIV: Last CD4 792, VL <48 copies. She was continued on her 
home HAART therapy.

# HCV: Last VL 733,000 IU/mL. She was last seen by Dr. ___ 
___ a week ago. She has apparently been a no-show for 
her follow-up appointments, but given her mild LFT 
abnormalities, it may be worthwhile to see if the patient as an 
outpatient would be willing to entertain a future visit with 
hepatology for further managemetnof her HCV

# RUL mass on CXR: On the patient's prior admission, a CXR from 
___ indicated that there was a persistent right upper lobe 
opacity in the paramediastinal location, which could be seen on 
the several prior radiographs including CT torso from ___, and while possibly representing a nonresolving infectious 
process, it also could also be a neoplastic focus. As an 
outpatient the patient may benefit from a CT Chest to exclude 
this possiblity.

# Asthma: Continued home medications

# Depression/anxiety: Very depressed and anxious, denies SI. 
Likely a huge contributor to her symptoms. She will need future 
follow-up by psychiatry, although from OMR notes it sounds as 
though she may have recently fired her psychiatrist.

# CODE STATUS: DNR/DNI confirmed
